turns.prompt: which small power station keeps a wi-fi router and modem running in a power outage and for how long
queries: EcoFlow River 3 245Wh Jackery Explorer 300 Plus 288Wh Anker SOLIX C300 DC specifications AC UPS 2026
turns.answer:
For keeping a Wi-Fi router and modem running during a power outage, I recommend a small portable power station with 200–300Wh of battery capacity.

Most home routers and cable modems together consume around 15–30 watts, so even a relatively small power station can keep your internet running for several hours.

Important: Will Wi-Fi stay connected without interruption?

If you want your modem and router to stay powered automatically when electricity fails, choose a power station with a UPS or pass-through backup feature. Not every portable power station supports this, and even UPS-capable models can briefly interrupt power during transfer.

Also, your internet provider's neighborhood equipment must remain operational during the outage.
